label: ANTs SmoothImage
description:
Gaussian smoothing or median filtering with a scalar/per-axis width.

The interface exposes the typed options listed below; the original installed-version help is retained in source references.

parameters.label: dimension
parameters.description: Image dimensionality. Match the actual input image.
parameters.usage: Image dimensionality. Match the actual input image. Unset optional values are not passed to the command.
parameters.software_default: The installed command decides omitted values; see the pinned help snapshot.

parameters.label: sigma
parameters.description: Gaussian sigma, or median radius in voxels; x separates axes.
parameters.usage: Gaussian sigma, or median radius in voxels; x separates axes. Unset optional values are not passed to the command.
parameters.software_default: The installed command decides omitted values; see the pinned help snapshot.

parameters.label: physical_units
parameters.description: Interpret sigma in physical spacing units.
parameters.usage: Interpret sigma in physical spacing units. Unset optional values are not passed to the command.
parameters.software_default: The installed command decides omitted values; see the pinned help snapshot.

parameters.label: median
parameters.description: Use median filter instead of Gaussian.
parameters.usage: Use median filter instead of Gaussian. Unset optional values are not passed to the command.
parameters.software_default: The installed command decides omitted values; see the pinned help snapshot.

input_slots.label: input
input_slots.description: Input image. Choose an existing file; the command never modifies it.

output_slots.label: output
output_slots.description: Native command output, saved in this run’s output directory. Gaussian smoothing or median filtering with a scalar/per-axis width. The output meaning depends on the input and selected operation. This generic image port does not certify anatomical labels, diffusion orientation, tissue fractions or spatial alignment.

omitted_options.other_options: Only the documented options below are exposed. Consult the installed-version help for other syntax; arbitrary arguments are not accepted.
